claims.text: Optimized Gd5(Si2Ge2) exhibits a superior magnetocaloric effect compared with conventional gadolinium.
Gd5(Si2Ge2) has magnetostructural coupling between magnetic ordering and crystallographic structure.
Magnetostructural coupling drives a first-order phase transition in Gd5(Si2Ge2).
The first-order phase transition of Gd5(Si2Ge2) occurs near room temperature.
A controlled, near-equiatomic Si-to-Ge ratio induces a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition in Gd5(Si2Ge2).
The specific Si/Ge ratio is responsible for strong coupling between magnetic ordering and crystallographic structure.
The first-order magnetostructural transition enhances magnetic entropy change by coupling lattice and magnetic degrees of freedom.
Gd5(Si2Ge2) couples lattice and magnetic degrees of freedom more effectively than unmodified gadolinium.
Gd5(Si2Ge2) will exhibit a significantly larger magnetic entropy change than pure or unoptimized gadolinium.
Gd5(Si2Ge2) will exhibit a larger adiabatic temperature change than pure or unoptimized gadolinium.
The proposed magnetocaloric enhancement is prominent around 300 K under applied magnetic fields of approximately 1–2 T.
The magnetocaloric effect may vary with slight compositional or processing differences.
Magnetostructural coupling effects in Gd-based compounds are known to produce qualitative magnetocaloric enhancement.
